paper.title: Prevalence, Thresholds, and Subgroup Performance Gaps in Clinical Prediction Models Across Five Public Datasets
paper.authors: Zavash Ghorbanpourbaboli, Arina Afshar, Elham Jangravi, Mohammed Ayoub Alaoui Mhamdi, Russell Butler

figures.title: Is the sensitivity gap distinguishable from zero?
figures.caption: Point = difference at the shared threshold; whiskers = 95% percentile CI from 1,000 bootstrap resamples drawn separately within each subgroup (paper §2).

figures.title: Prevalence standardization
figures.caption: Holding each group's sensitivity and specificity fixed, PPV is recomputed at a common prevalence. The curve shows how much of the PPV gap is just base rates.

figures.title: Threshold dependence
figures.caption: Each metric's gap as the shared operating threshold moves. Shrinking one gap can grow another.

figures.title: Same data, different defensible choices
figures.caption: Point estimates re-run under every combination of threshold rule and data-preparation choices (fast gradient-boosting model). Orange = negative gap, blue = positive.

compare.note: Paper's predictor set, age bands and patient-level resampling; model hyperparameters are ours.

compare.paper: BRFSS M−F +0.101 → +0.016; CCHS M−F +0.053 → −0.005 (point estimate only; interval spans zero)
